claims.text: http.get(Uri) sends a GET request and returns a Future<http.Response>; http.Response has statusCode and body (String).
claims.source_hint: pub.dev http 1.6 API docs: get, Response

claims.text: jsonDecode (dart:convert) turns JSON text into Dart values: List for arrays, Map<String, dynamic> for objects.
ApiClient.fetchProducts awaits http.get('$baseUrl/products'), throws Exception if statusCode != 200, decodes the body as List<dynamic> and maps each item through Product.fromJson.
ApiClient.baseUrl is http://localhost:8080/api/v1, going through Caddy.
Product.fromJson reads json['id'] as int, json['name'] as String, json['priceVnd'] as int; GET /api/v1/products returns ProductDto(Id, Name, PriceVnd) serialized as camelCase id, name, priceVnd.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: DonHang.App/lib/models.dart:3-15; DonHang.Api/Dtos.cs:5; ASP.NET Core default camelCase JSON

claims.text: In Dart, `as` throws a TypeError when the value has the wrong type (C#'s `as` returns null instead); an exception thrown inside an async function completes its Future with an error, delivered to whoever awaits it.
claims.source_hint: Dart language docs: type test/cast operators (as); async functions and Futures

claims.text: await inside an async Dart function suspends only that function; on the web the browser performs the request without blocking the page's thread.
claims.source_hint: Dart docs: asynchronous programming (async/await); pub.dev http (BrowserClient on web)

claims.text: Checking the status before reading the body, and typed mapping with checked casts, make mismatches fail loudly.
Dart's async/await model is similar to C#'s.
The API builds ProductDto(p.Id, p.Name, p.PriceVnd) from typed fields and serializes it to JSON; the client does the reverse.
DonHang.App lists http in its pubspec.yaml dependencies; Product.fromJson is a factory constructor that reads the Map and calls the ordinary Product(...) constructor.
